hints: Every query is answered by the same scan of line. Can you work out the next taller value for every number in line in one pass, then just look the queries up?
Use a monotonic decreasing stack while walking line. Numbers on the stack are still waiting for something bigger. Save each answer in a HashMap from value to its next taller value.

1. Create an empty stack and an empty map.
  2. For each x in line: while the stack top is smaller than x, pop it and record map[top] = x.
  3. Push x.
  4. For each query q, the answer is map[q], or -1 if it is missing.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each query, find its position in line, then scan to the right for the first larger value.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass over line with a decreasing stack fills a map of next taller values; each query is a map lookup.

explain: Take line = [5,3,8,1,9]. Push 5, then 3 (stack 5,3). When 8 arrives it is bigger than 3 and 5, so both pop with answer 8. Push 8, then 1. When 9 arrives it pops 1 and 8, both getting 9. Number 9 stays on the stack, so it has no answer. Queries [3,8,5] give [8,9,8]. The stack is always decreasing from bottom to top, and each number is pushed and popped at most once, so the pass is linear.
recognize: 'First value to the right that is larger' → monotonic stack.
